headline: An independent maths exam found the best AI system solved nine of ten research problems, while the best open-weight model solved none.
score_reason: Pool score 6 kept: an independent, controlled test, though only ten problems and some labs did not take part.
summary: Scientific American reports that First Proof, an independent project of leading mathematicians that tests publicly available AI models, released its third results on 14 Oct 2026: ProofCouncil, a system combining several agents on OpenAI's GPT 6 Astra, solved nine of ten research problems to a standard graders called acceptable with minor revisions. The best open-weight model, meaning one whose inner workings are public, Kimi K3, solved none, and Mohammed Abouzaid, a Stanford University mathematician on the team, calls the gap very large.
importance_line: Mathematicians who need privacy or cannot pay for frontier models see that open alternatives are far behind, though the test has only ten problems and Google did not take part.
notes: OpenAI's newest internal model was excluded from the test because it is not openly available.
